questions.question: A closed system is one that exchanges with its surroundings:
Chemical equilibrium is the state in which:
options: The concentrations of reactants and products are equal
The forward and reverse reaction rates are equal, so concentrations remain constant

questions.question: Equilibrium is called DYNAMIC because:
options: Both forward and reverse reactions continue at the particle level while totals stay constant
The reaction speeds up over time

questions.question: Equilibrium can only be established in a closed system because:
options: Energy must not enter the system
Open systems are always too cold
Catalysts only work in sealed flasks
If products escape, the reverse reaction loses its ingredients and the rates can never balance

questions.question: Le Chatelier's principle states that a disturbed equilibrium will:
options: Return to exactly its original state
Stop reacting until the disturbance is removed
Favour the reaction that opposes the disturbance, establishing a new equilibrium

questions.question: For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (forward exothermic), RAISING the temperature will:
options: Favour the endothermic reverse reaction, decreasing the ammonia yield
Favour the forward reaction, increasing the yield
Have no effect on the equilibrium position

questions.question: Increasing the pressure on N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ shifts the equilibrium:
options: Toward the reactants, which have more gas moles
Toward the ammonia side, which has fewer gas moles

questions.question: A catalyst added to an equilibrium system:
options: Shifts the equilibrium toward the products
Speeds both reactions equally, reaching the same equilibrium sooner

questions.question: On a concentration-time graph, an instantaneous vertical jump in ONE species' line indicates:
options: That species was suddenly added or removed
The volume of the vessel changed

questions.question: A disturbance where ALL gaseous concentrations jump at the same instant indicates:
options: A change in the vessel's volume (pressure)

questions.question: A temperature change appears on a concentration-time graph as:
options: A vertical jump in every line
A vertical jump in one line only
Nothing — temperature cannot affect the graph
No instant jump, only curves bending toward new levels

questions.question: After more reactant is added, the system settles at concentrations that are:
options: Exactly the original values — the disturbance is fully undone
New equilibrium values — the disturbance is only partially opposed

questions.question: In the Kc expression, the concentrations that never appear are those of:
For H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI with equilibrium concentrations H₂ = 0,1; I₂ = 0,1; HI = 0,8 mol·dm⁻³, Kc equals:
A very small Kc (much less than 1) tells you that at equilibrium:
options: Mostly reactants remain — the forward reaction barely proceeded

questions.question: The ONLY change that alters the value of Kc for a given reaction is:

subtopics.title: The Shop Where the Crowd Never Changes

questions.question: In the shop analogy, the constant crowd of 200 with 40 entering and 40 leaving per minute represents:
options: Dynamic equilibrium — constant concentrations with ongoing two-way reaction

questions.question: "Constant does not mean equal" reminds you that at equilibrium:
options: The reactant and product concentrations may be very different, but neither is changing
The forward rate exceeds the reverse rate
The system must contain equal moles of everything

questions.question: The "missing back wall" through which shoppers wander off represents:
options: An open system, in which equilibrium cannot establish

questions.question: Every equilibrium response to a disturbance is:
options: A complete reversal of the disturbance
A partial counteraction — the push is never fully undone

questions.question: Writing "plus heat" on the product side of an exothermic equation helps because raising the temperature then reads as:
options: Adding a product, so the system leans back toward reactants

questions.question: Factories continuously remove product from equilibrium reactions because:
options: Each removal drags the equilibrium toward making more product
The product would poison the catalyst
It raises the value of Kc

questions.question: "Greasing the pivot" — the catalyst — changes:
options: The final tilt of the see-saw
Only how fast balance is reached, not where it settles
The number of gas moles on each side

questions.question: A huge Kc — in the thousands — means:
options: The vessel holds almost all products at equilibrium

questions.question: The four bookkeeping lines for a Kc calculation are:
options: Initial moles, change, remaining moles, divide by volume for concentrations

questions.question: The most expensive shortcut in a Kc calculation is:
options: Substituting raw moles instead of dividing by the vessel's volume first

questions.question: Heating an EXOTHERMIC reaction changes its "score" by:
options: Lowering Kc — products lose ground at the new temperature
